question: A bookseller sells a novel for Y and makes a loss of 15%. To clear old stock, he decides to mark the novel at 0.8Y. He then allows a further discount of 5% on this marked price. What will be the percentage loss that he will incur on this clearance sale?
solution:
**Given:**

Selling price at first = Y

Loss = 15%

Clearance marked price = 0.8Y

Further discount = 5%

**Formula used:**

CP = SP ÷ (1 − loss%)

New SP = MP × (1 − discount%)

Loss% = ((CP − New SP) ÷ CP) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = Y ÷ 0.85

⇒ New SP = 0.8Y × 0.95

⇒ New SP = 0.76Y

⇒ Loss% = (CP − New SP) ÷ CP × 100

⇒ Loss% = ( (Y/0.85) − 0.76Y ) ÷ (Y/0.85) × 100

⇒ Loss% = ( 1/0.85 − 0.76 ) ÷ (1/0.85 ) × 100

⇒ 1/0.85 ≈ 1.176

⇒ Loss% = (1.176 − 0.76) ÷ 1.176 × 100

⇒ Loss% = 0.416 ÷ 1.176 × 100

⇒ Loss% ≈ 35.36%

**∴ The bookseller incurs approximately 35.36% loss in the clearance sale.**
